_descriptor_type: A type of descriptor. One of 'simulation', 'trace', and 'perf'.
_architecture: A name of the available architectures (PARAMS.<architecture>) found in scarab repository, which defines the machine parameters of the default configuration.
_experiment: The name of the experiment. scarab-infra will create a new folder named containing all files needed to execute the simulation in the <ROOT_DIR>/simulations/<experiment> directory. The folder will also contain all generated simulation statistics/outputs.
_workload_manager: manual: run each exp scenario with all the simpoints at a time, slurm: Slurm schedules simulations based on its policy
_root_dir: Root directory mounted into the docker container home, for instance, the user's home directory
_application_dir: The path to the benchmark application directory used for tracing or simulation.
_scarab_path: The path to the scarab repository that contains the scarab binary used to run the experiment. REQUIRES the build with the LLC three-arm duel (--td_combined_l1_set_duel and the td_combined_l1_duel_* knobs) AND the earlier fix that added TD_COMBINED_ON_L1 to the topdown measurement gates. Without the latter no fraction is ever measured at the LLC, every line inserts at basic, and every config here reads identically.
_traces_dir: The local directory containing all simpointed traces
_top_simpoint: Run only top 3 simpoints stored in 'workloads_top_simp.json'.
_simulations: Explores the three-arm set duel on the combined LLC policy. Arms: DEPTH (instruction pinned at -32, data OFF / -16 / -32), THRESH (0.5 vs 0.7 applied to both class gates together), BASIC (unmarked insertion RRPV 2 / 3 / 4). Group 0 always runs the incumbent so ties hold it, every other group is a one-coordinate probe off it, and each window the winning group moves exactly that coordinate. Two questions. (1) WHICH ARMS EARN THEIR SETS -- arm_* enable each subset; every arm costs leader sets that run a non-selected policy, so an arm that never wins is pure overhead. Leader totals at 16 sets/group on 2048 sets: all three 6 groups = 96 sets (4.7%), depth-only 3 = 48 (2.3%), depth+basic 5 = 80 (3.9%), none 1 = 16 (0.8%). (2) WHICH SELECTION METRIC -- metric 0 minimises demand misses on the leader sets (the classic DRRIP criterion), metric 1 maximises PROTECTED HITS, counting only hits on lines that were marked at insert. Metric 1 asks 'is the protection I bought being reused' rather than 'did this arm miss least', and the two genuinely disagree: an arm that marks very few lines can score well on protected hits while missing more overall, so metric 1 should favour narrower, more confident marking. Every arm combination is run under both metrics. static_i32d16 is the no-duel control at the incumbent's seed configuration.
_configurations: baseline is byte-identical to td_combined_llc_data / _instr (LLC tree-PLRU, --l1_cache_repl_policy 21) so all the LLC runs share a reference. Naming: arm_<arms>_m<metric>; d=depth, t=thresh, b=basic. A disabled arm drops its probe groups AND pins its coordinate -- depth to the static --td_fe_rrip_min_rrpv / --td_load_rrip_min_rrpv, threshold to the static gates, basic to --marked_rrip_basic_rrpv. Every config therefore also carries those static values, which is what the disabled arms fall back to; they are set to the duel's own seed point (instr -32, data -16, gates 0.7 / 0.5, basic 3) so enabling an arm changes only what varies, never the starting point. Window is 100k retired instructions throughout.

baseline._params: LLC tree-PLRU (REPL_PLRU_TREE, 21). Shared reference with the other LLC runs.

static_i32d16._params: No-duel control at the duel's seed configuration: instr -32, data -16, gates 0.7 / 0.5, basic 3. Everything below must beat this to justify spending leader sets at all.

arm_d_m0._params: DEPTH arm only, metric = demand misses. 3 groups, 48 leader sets (2.3%).

arm_d_m1._params: DEPTH arm only, metric = protected hits.

arm_dt_m0._params: DEPTH + THRESH, metric = demand misses. 4 groups, 64 leader sets (3.1%).

arm_dt_m1._params: DEPTH + THRESH, metric = protected hits. The pairing where metric 1 should bite hardest: raising the gate marks fewer lines, which hurts raw misses but can raise the protected-hit rate.

arm_db_m0._params: DEPTH + BASIC, metric = demand misses. 5 groups, 80 leader sets (3.9%).

arm_dtb_m0._params: All three arms, metric = demand misses. 6 groups, 96 leader sets (4.7%) -- the full mechanism.

arm_dtb_m1._params: All three arms, metric = protected hits.

arm_dtb_m0_g8._params: All three arms, misses, 8 sets per group = 48 leader sets (2.3%) instead of 96. Halves the sampling tax so more followers cash in the winner; noisier per-group scores. Pairs with arm_dtb_m0 to separate 'the arms help' from 'the leader tax hurts'.

arm_dtb_m0_w20k._params: All three arms, misses, 20k-instruction window instead of 100k. Coordinate descent moves one axis per window, so a shorter window converges faster but on noisier evidence -- with 3 arms it takes several windows to traverse the space at all.

_collect_stats: Stats collection settings for ./sci --collect-stats. configs: optional list of configuration names to collect (null or omitted = all configurations).
_visualize: 'IPC' is the TARGET-ONLY figure (Periodic_*), matching plot_stat_change_multi.py's default; pass --full-sim for the Cumulative_* figure. The two ONPATH splits matter here because the depth arm trades the classes against each other -- data OFF / -16 / -32 at fixed instruction -32 -- so L1_MISS_ONPATH_IFETCH and L1_MISS_ONPATH_DFETCH show which side the duel settled on, which the total cannot. Note 'L1_*' is Scarab's LLC naming, not the L1 data cache (DCACHE_*). When comparing m0 against m1, expect the metric to change WHERE the duel lands rather than how well it duels: metric 1 should push toward narrower marking, so look for it trading a small IFETCH/DFETCH miss increase for better IPC (or not, which is equally informative).
_mem: Memory scheduling and collection settings for Slurm jobs.
